🇲🇽🗳️ <u>PAN moves to lock Morena's Santiago Nieto out of Querétaro's Congress</u>

In PAN-governed Querétaro, the panista head of the state Congress moved to physically bar Santiago Nieto — Morena's coordinator for the defense of the Fourth Transformation — from entering the chamber. Nieto called it "inadmissible in democratic terms… a personalized gag order, a display of authoritarianism and repression against the advance of Morena and the 4T," and vowed to challenge it "to the last consequences."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Declassified files: the PRI's secret police even spied on its own</u>

Newly surfaced DFS archives — Mexico's Cold-War political police, with reports signed by spymasters like Miguel Nazar Haro — show the old regime didn't just hunt dissidents: from 1975 it tracked the "loyalty" of its own rising figures, logging a young Roberto Madrazo's rallies as it vetted him for the machine. The surveillance state the PRI sold to Mexico as democracy.
banner: DFS FILES: PRI SPIED ON ITS OWN

🇲🇽🌱 <u>Mexico seals a beachfront build that bulldozed protected dunes</u>

Federal inspectors from Profepa shut down a construction site in Chabihau, Yucatán after heavy machinery destroyed 669 m² of protected coastal dune — tearing out threatened button mangrove and wild cotton, habitat of a threatened iguana — with zero environmental authorization. "Those responsible did not exhibit any authorization, permit, license or environmental exemption," the agency reported, placing seals on the works under NOM-022.

🇲🇽🎖️ <u>216 years on, Mexico "will never be a colony or protectorate of anyone"</u>

President Sheinbaum led the Independence Day military parade as 99 aircraft flew over the Zócalo simultaneously for the first time in history — 93 Air Force and 6 National Guard — with 15,458 troops marching below. Her line to the crowd on the 216th anniversary of the Grito: Mexico "no será nunca colonia ni protectorado de nadie."

🇲🇽🥑 <u>Mexico ties every avocado export to proof its workers have rights</u>

As of Sept 15, no Mexican avocado can ship to the US unless the grower holds a new Certificado Laboral — verified through the government's VELAGRO platform, which cross-checks each shipment against IMSS to confirm field hands are formalized and insured. The pilot starts in Michoacán and Jalisco and expands to berries next, part of formalizing some 200,000 farmworkers. The world's top avocado supplier now sells the "green gold" on one condition: the people who pick it get paid and covered.
banner: AVOCADO EXPORTS TIED TO LABOR RIGHTS

text:
🇲🇽📊 <u>ONE MONTH OF MINIMUM WAGE NOW BEATS THE BASIC BASKET</u>

Per INEGI data reported by El Economista, a city resident needed 4,905 pesos in August for the basic basket of food and services, with the food basket up 4.5% year-on-year. The context that matters: after a real minimum-wage rise of more than 135% since 2018, one month of minimum-wage work now covers that basket outright — the opposite of the neoliberal decades, when the daily minimum bought barely a sliver of it.
banner: MIN WAGE NOW BEATS BASIC BASKET

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE MACHINE BEHIND LATIN AMERICA’S FAR RIGHT</u>

A transnational disinformation operation that fabricated audio smearing Mexico’s Nov 15 protest and targets President Sheinbaum runs through Argentine operative Fernando Cerimedo — now jailed in Bolivia — and his Miami-linked firms, which he admits build fake bot accounts to “manufacture relevance” for candidates like Milei, Bolsonaro and Bolivia’s Rodrigo Paz before laundering it through friendly media.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>CNDH: MEXICO MUST REGULATE AI — AND STORE ITS OWN DATA</u>

Mexico’s National Human Rights Commission is pushing for AI rules built on data sovereignty: national infrastructure to store and process Mexicans’ data at home, home-grown AI talent, and democratic oversight instead of corporate self-regulation — warning that leaving it to Big Tech risks “algorithmic discrimination” and the concentration of computational power in a few foreign hands.
banner: CNDH: REGULATE AI, KEEP DATA HOME

text:
🇲🇽🛢️ <u>FIVE SOVEREIGNTIES: HOW MEXICO IS DEFENDING ITS INDEPENDENCE</u>

Sheinbaum’s Second Report frames independence as five sovereignties defended with data: public debt down to 51% of GDP, eight new exploratory oil wells drilling as deep as 8,482 meters, 70+ tons of native seeds handed to 5,000 small farmers (lifting corn and bean yields at least 20%), and a national rail network now spanning 29,042 km. As she put it, “to preserve our freedoms, we must defend national sovereignty.”
